html:
SMTO-LLM-0067 — The model server is taking too long to get ready

GUID: 2c81ba45-bf53-57e6-89ff-43683110b359
Slug: local-ai-start-timeout
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: local_ai

What happened

  • SMTO started the model server, but it wasn't ready before SMTO stopped waiting. It may still be loading, so starting another copy could make things worse.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait a few minutes, then ask SMTO to show the status of this Local AI runtime on that Gateway, the helper program SMTO uses on that computer. Large models often take longer to load than SMTO waits, and it may become ready on its own.
  2. If the status shows ready, use it as it is; don't start it again. It is already running, so a second start would only compete for the same memory.
  3. If it's still starting, ask SMTO to show its logs and check whether loading is making progress. Steady progress means it's just slow; repeated errors mean something needs fixing.
  4. If it loads normally but slowly, raise startup_timeout (up to 300 seconds) in the profile in Parameter Store and select Save for next time. A longer wait lets future starts finish without this error.

What success looks like

  • The runtime's status shows ready and the model server answers.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and the log text, and send them to the person who manages that Gateway. Don't start another copy while this one may still be loading. Don't stop programs on that computer that SMTO didn't start.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The spawned runtime did not pass its health check within the profile's startup_timeout (default 60 seconds, maximum 300); the process may still be starting and was not stopped.

What this means

  • The startup loop exhausted its deadline without observing a live process and successful health check together; it does not automatically prove the process stopped. Local AI management belongs to the selected Gateway and accepted profile. Starting a runtime does not activate it for the controller; recorded execution and unknown-effect facts determine whether reconciliation is required.

Why this can happen

  • The startup loop exhausted its deadline without observing a live process and successful health check together; it does not automatically prove the process stopped.

How to diagnose it

  • Read the existing runtime ID and its log/health state; distinguish continuing startup from an exited process.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the existing runtime with local_ai.runtime, health and logs before any lifecycle action. If it is still loading, wait for ready; if logs show steady progress, raise startup_timeout (1 to 300 seconds) in the profile. Do not start a second instance for the same profile.
  • Inspect the existing runtime first; adjust the profile startup allowance only if observed startup progress justifies it.

Retry and execution caution

  • Only after exact state reconciliation.

How to verify the fix

  • The original runtime reaches ready or a conclusive stopped/exited state before another launch decision.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations or stop externally owned processes.

Technical notes

  • Local AI management belongs to the selected Gateway and accepted profile. Starting a runtime does not activate it for the controller; recorded execution and unknown-effect facts determine whether reconciliation is required.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
